title: QUIC RFC 9000 Connection Close Packet-Level Emission
purpose: Describe how the runtime chooses packet protection levels for locally generated CONNECTION_CLOSE frames before and after handshake confirmation.
design_summary: The runtime now formats CONNECTION_CLOSE payloads according to the packet number space that will carry them. After handshake confirmation, a close is emitted as a protected 1-RTT packet when 1-RTT protect material is available. Before confirmation, the runtime emits every available close level that can be constructed: server Initial, Handshake, and 1-RTT. Initial and Handshake close packets use new close-only long-header builders in the handshake coordinator, while 1-RTT close continues to use the short-header application-data builder.
data_and_state_considerations: Close emission remains active-path scoped and consumes anti-amplification budget per datagram. The runtime does not track CONNECTION_CLOSE packets for retransmission. Packet protection availability gates each emitted level; if no protected close packet can be built, the runtime preserves the existing bare close-payload fallback used by legacy establishment tests.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Application CONNECTION_CLOSE frames are downgraded to transport CONNECTION_CLOSE frames only for Initial and Handshake packets.
When downgrading an application close below 1-RTT, the runtime clears the reason phrase and uses APPLICATION_ERROR.
Server pre-confirmation close attempts include both Initial and Handshake packets when their protection material is available.
Pre-confirmation 1-RTT close is emitted only when 1-RTT protect material has already been installed.
Post-confirmation close keeps the application close frame type in 1-RTT packets.
alternatives_considered: Coalesce Initial, Handshake, and 1-RTT close packets into a single UDP datagram; deferred because separate send effects prove packet-level behavior without changing the existing send-effect contract.
Use the CRYPTO packet builders with empty CRYPTO payloads; rejected because existing builders intentionally require CRYPTO data and close-only packets need a control-frame builder.
Downgrade all close payloads before 1-RTT regardless of packet space; rejected because 1-RTT packets are permitted to carry application close frames.
risks: The slice does not implement close-packet coalescing.
Legacy bare close fallback remains for states where no protected close packet can be constructed.
The slice does not broaden CONNECTION_CLOSE retransmission behavior; close packets remain outside recovery repair.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers local CONNECTION_CLOSE packet-level emission and downgrade behavior. It does not claim new peer close parsing, close retransmission, or post-close timer behavior beyond the existing lifecycle slice.
